items.question: The trader says two rules of thumb, RSI(9) 60/40 and volume above 3x SMA(9), may be changed if that makes the analysis more accurate. On current data neither has outcome evidence: the volume vote has never fired live because it reads the in-progress bar, and the RSI vote was never read alone; momentum votes lean negative in one session but did not replicate. What should be done now?

options.label: (a)
options.text: make only the mechanism fixes that need no outcome data (closed-bar volume on the engine's dynamic threshold; RSI levels on 3-minute bars mapped to the same market state), and run a pre-registered, split-half outcome study on 21 months of closed bars from the history store before choosing any new level or replacement measure

options.label: (b)
options.text: pick new levels now from the existing live book by searching for the best-performing values

options.label: (c)
options.text: keep both rules exactly as they are

items.rationale: (b) fits levels on a small book where the volume vote never fired and the RSI vote was never isolated, which is overfitting. (c) keeps a dead volume vote and a resolution mismatch. (a) fixes what is provably wrong and lets the data choose the rest with a holdout.
